definitions.explanation: to firmly refuse or reject something; stronger than simply declining

examples.japanese: {申|もう}し{出|で}を{拒否|きょひ}した。
{入国|にゅうこく}を{拒否|きょひ}される。
examples.english: To be denied entry to the country.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{質問|しつもん}への{回答|かいとう}を{拒否|きょひ}した。
examples.english: She refused to answer the question.

notes:
USAGE:
- 〜を{拒否|きょひ}する (to refuse/reject ~)
- {拒否|きょひ}{反応|はんのう} (rejection reaction - medical)
- {拒否権|きょひけん} (veto power, right of refusal)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {要求|ようきゅう}を{拒否|きょひ}する (to refuse a demand)
- {署名|しょめい}を{拒否|きょひ}する (to refuse to sign)
- {出席|しゅっせき}を{拒否|きょひ}する (to refuse to attend)

NUANCE:
{拒否|きょひ} is stronger and more formal than {断|ことわ}る (to decline). It implies a firm, sometimes defiant refusal.

RELATED:
- {断|ことわ}る (to decline - softer)
- {却下|きゃっか} (rejection - of proposals/appeals)
- {受|う}け{入|い}れる (to accept - antonym)
